standard_prerequisites.name: Tree of tuples
standard_prerequisites.statement: The labelled tree T_A of a structure is the tree of its finite tuples ordered by extension.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the tree on which the tuples live.

standard_prerequisites.name: Somewhat and entirely incomparable points
standard_prerequisites.statement: A point is somewhat comparable to a tuple c when some non-root prefix of the point is a prefix of some entry of c, and entirely incomparable when it is not; a tuple is entirely incomparable when all of its points are.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on the two tuples and is retained inside the card as context.

standard_prerequisites.name: Back-and-forth relations of the tree
standard_prerequisites.statement: The relations <=_alpha are the back-and-forth relations of the labelled tree, defined by the usual game of rank alpha.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the relation the lemma compares.

core_obligations: Prove the statement by transfinite induction on alpha, with the zero and limit cases immediate and only the successor step left (source lines 351-355).
One direction of the successor step is immediate, since the relation between tuples is inherited by anything appended to both sides (source lines 356-357).
For the other direction, take an arbitrary extension and split it into the points somewhat comparable to the fixed tuple and the points entirely incomparable to it (source lines 358-362).

Use the winning response for the original pair, move it by an automorphism that fixes the first tuple and sends the fixed tuple to something entirely incomparable, and rearrange tuples to read off the required relation at the successor rank (source lines 363-366).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the transfinite induction, leaving the successor step.
The easy direction of the successor step.
Split an arbitrary extension against the fixed tuple.
Transport the winning response and rearrange tuples.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 346-349: in the tree of tuples of a structure, for tuples a and b entirely incomparable to a tuple p, appending p to both sides preserves the rank alpha back-and-forth relation in both directions. The statement reduces a comparison of longer tuples to a comparison of shorter ones, and the proof (source lines 350-367) must establish the nontrivial direction of the successor step of a transfinite induction: it splits an arbitrary extension into the part somewhat comparable to p and the part entirely incomparable to it, uses the winning response for the shorter pair, moves that response by an automorphism fixing the first tuple and sending p to an entirely incomparable tuple, and then rearranges the tuples to produce the relation required at the successor rank. What is being compared, and how the incomparability hypothesis is used, is not visible in the statement.
